newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - roasters weather the storm.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - roasters weather the storm.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market remained sluggish this week, as roasters continued to balk at paying lofty premiums for spot parcels, traders said.
With the spot December futures contract due to expire in a few weeks, processors appeared content to wait for shipments to pick up from Latin America.
"Roasters are taking in deliveries, waiting for deliveries and waiting for December to go away," one trader said.
Ongoing near-term supply concerns have kept December's premium to second-month March near a hefty 9.00 cents, bolstering cash differentials as well.
While their inventories have diminished substantially, traders said end-users have tightened their belts, waiting to price against second-position March.
"Roasters who learned to live with just-in-time inventory got stung in September, October and the first half of November," one said. "But the pendulum is swinging the other way."
But with roasters taking -- and still waiting for -- overdue deliveries, traders said a rebound in consumer inventories was unlikely until January.
"There will be more coffee available first quarter of 1997," a trader said, "but a huge build-up in stocks not expected."

Colombian MAMs for spot delivery continued to command stiff premiums, netting 28 to 30 cents over the CSCE December contract this week. For December shipment, MAMS were heard at 13 cents over March FOB.
Elsewhere, Brazil Santos 2/3s, due early December, traded at three cents under March, while spot strictly-soft "European-prep" Costa Rican coffee garnered 25 cents over "C".
CSCE December coffee rose 1.00 cent a lb Friday, to settle at 118.25. March ended 0.65 higher, at 109.50.
